newsitem.title: USA: Salty Kraft product may pose blood pressure risk - study.
newsitem.headline: Salty Kraft product may pose blood pressure risk - study.

text.p: Lunchables, a package of meat, cheese and crackers sold by the Kraft unit of Philip Morris Cos Inc, contains enough salt to raise blood pressure in certain laboratory rats and may pose a health risk to some humans, a study released Sunday said.

Lunchables "may be a dangerous snack for families with a history of high blood pressure," said Dr. Clarence Grim of the Medical College of Wisconsin in a statement released here at an American College of Cardiology conference.
In reply, Kraft called the Wisconsin study "junk science at its worst."
"The whole premise of the study is preposterous ... This is yet another attempt to unnecessarily frighten American consumers about the food they eat," Kraft said in a statement.
The Wisconsin medical resarchers said their study used three groups of salt-sensitive rats, a special breed "thought to be a good model for salt toxicity in humans."

One group was fed ground Lunchables containing ham, Swiss cheese and crackers. A second group was fed a ham-cheese-and-crackers diet with half the salt level of the first, and the third group was fed regular low-salt rat chow, which has about one-fifth the salt of Lunchables, researchers said.

"The rats on the Lunchables diet had a 20-percent increase in blood pressure compared to the third group fed rat chow, and a 10-percent increase compared to the second group fed a diet containing 50 percent less salt," the researchers reported.
Along with raised blood pressure, the rats on the ground Lunchables diet also experienced enlarged hearts and kidneys, the researchers said.
Kraft said Lunchables comes in 28 different varieties.

The researchers said the one they used contained 1,780 milligrams of salt, near the 2,000 milligram-level likely to cause high blood pressure in salt-sensitive people and equal to 74 percent of the daily recommended adult salt intake.

"These snacks should be considered dangerous for persons with high blood pressure, or those who have a history of high blood pressure in their families, especially African Americans, as these snacks alone provide enough salt to cause high blood pressure," Dr. Grim said.
He said Lunchables should carry a label containing "warnings of the toxic effects of salt in people who have high blood pressure or who come from a family with high blood pressure."

Kraft said, "This study is junk science at its worst -- feed four rats all the Lunchables they can eat for three weeks and then use that to make a sweeping conclusion. Nobody would eat a diet of all Lunchables or any other single food."
The products' sodium content is listed on the label and is within government recommendations for the daily value of sodium, Kraft said.

The company added, "Sodium consumption is a concern for a small population. Certainly, people who have been put on a sodium-restricted diet on doctor's advice should be aware of sodium levels. In such cases, Lunchables may not be the right product for them."
